course.name: Interfaces: Pages, Widgets & Chat
course.description: Your flows work. Now give them a face — pages, widgets, routes, and chat surfaces your team can actually use.
course.longDescription: The support team is never going to open Studio — so ship them a console instead. Across seven lessons you build the interfaces of a real support app on Flow-Like's A2UI model: design a live operations dashboard in the visual Page Builder, extract a reusable health card into a Widget with exposed properties and page-bound events, brand the built-in Chat UI without losing its AI disclosure, give every surface a route, and wire every click to a flow through Events pinned to safe versions. Ends with a ship-day assessment on the complete console.

modules.title: From flows to product
modules.description: Meet the A2UI model behind every surface, and give each surface an address.

lessons.title: Where does your app meet its users?

challenges.prompt: You open the Support Operations Dashboard in the builder and peek at Dev Mode. What are you actually looking at?
challenges.explanation: An A2UI surface is data: one root component plus a flat, ID-connected list of typed components. The renderer maps that data onto allowlisted React components at display time — which makes 'generated React source' tempting but wrong. There is no code artifact to edit or recompile; Dev Mode shows the interface itself.

options.label: Structured data: a tree of typed components referenced by ID
Generated React source code you can edit and recompile
A rendered snapshot — the real interface lives in the flow
HTML markup exported from the canvas

challenges.prompt: Which of these render from the same A2UI component model?
challenges.explanation: Pages, Widgets, and interfaces a flow returns at runtime all render from one declarative component model — that is the point of A2UI. The flow board canvas is Studio's own editor, not an A2UI surface you author, and the Events workspace is part of the app shell.

options.label: Pages
Widgets
Interfaces a flow returns at runtime
The flow board canvas in Studio
The Events workspace list

challenges.prompt: You arrange the dashboard visually, ask FlowPilot to restyle it, then fine-tune one property in Dev Mode. What is the result?
challenges.explanation: All three authoring paths — visual builder, FlowPilot, and Dev Mode — modify the same component model, so edits accumulate on one surface in any order. 'FlowPilot replaces your manual edits' is the tempting one: FlowPilot works with the active builder surface and revises it in place; it does not produce a competing copy, and neither does Dev Mode.

options.label: One surface — all three paths edit the same component model, in any order
FlowPilot's version replaces your manual edits, so finish by hand
Dev Mode edits a separate JSON copy you must sync back to the canvas
After a JSON edit, the visual builder becomes read-only for that page

lessons.title: Routes: every surface gets an address

challenges.prompt: Who owns the path /support?
challenges.explanation: Routes are stored as path-to-Event mappings: the UI Event owns the address and decides which interface opens there. The Page is the tempting owner — but a page has no route setting at all. It becomes reachable when a Page-target Event carries the path.

options.label: The UI Event that opens the surface
The Page — the route is a page setting
The flow that powers the page
The app's navigation menu

challenges.prompt: You create a Page-target Event for the Escalation Console and type /triage as its route. Look at @RoutesOverview — what's the problem?
challenges.explanation: Routes must be unique within the app, and the screenshot shows /triage already assigned to the Triage selected request Quick Action. 'Quick Actions don't occupy routes' is the tempting out — but a Quick Action is a UI Event like any other, and the badge next to it is exactly that route claim.

options.label: /triage already belongs to the Triage quick action — routes must be unique within the app
Nothing — Quick Actions don't occupy routes, so /triage is free
A page route must contain the page's name
Two events can't target the same flow

challenges.prompt: Which statements about routes are true?
challenges.explanation: Backend-only Events (Cron, API) run without any route, and a red No route badge marks a UI Event that is unreachable by path. The tempting extra is prefix matching — but routes match as configured, so /chat answers /chat and nothing else. And a Page is never openable by path without a UI Event in front of it.

options.label: Backend-only Events work without any route
A red No route badge means the Event can't be reached by path
A Page can be opened by path without a UI Event
Paths match by prefix, so /chat also answers /chat/settings

modules.title: Build the surfaces
modules.description: Pages, reusable widgets, and a branded chat — the console takes shape.

challenges.prompt: In @PageBuilder the Open tickets card is selected. Where do you change its Title from "Open tickets" to "Open requests"?
challenges.explanation: Selecting a component fills the Inspector, and its Props tab is where the Title lives — you can see it holding 'Open tickets' in the screenshot. Dev Mode could also change it, but the distractor's claim is backwards: the visual builder edits every component property; JSON is the optional path, not the required one.

options.label: In the Inspector panel on the right
In Dev Mode — the visual builder can't edit component properties
In the Hierarchy tab
In the flow that owns the page

challenges.prompt: The card's title never changes, but the 24 must track the live queue. How do you configure the two properties?
challenges.explanation: Fixed presentation stays literal; live facts get bindings, so the flow keeps them fresh. 'Bind both' is the tempting overcorrection — literals render at runtime just fine, and binding a static title adds indirection for nothing. Page Settings → Behavior schedules refresh events; it isn't where a value is stored.

options.label: Title as a literal, the number as a bound value the flow keeps fresh
Bind both — properties must be bound to render at runtime
Keep both literal and re-edit the page whenever the numbers change
Store the number in Page Settings → Behavior

challenges.prompt: The dashboard should refresh its stats every minute while someone is looking at it. Where does that belong?
challenges.explanation: Page Settings → Behavior runs Flow events on load, unload, or at an interval — a once-a-minute refresh belongs there, and a cached page can even show its last state while the load event refreshes. Cron is the tempting answer: it does schedule flow runs, but as a backend trigger it fires whether or not anyone has the page open; the page's interval event is scoped to the surface being viewed.

options.label: Page Settings → Behavior: run a flow event at an interval
A Cron event on the flow — schedules are backend work
A refresh loop added in Dev Mode JSON
Nothing — autosave keeps pages current

challenges.prompt: @WidgetsOverview shows one configurable property: Card title. What does that let a page author do?
challenges.explanation: An exposed property maps an instance-facing option (Card title) to one internal component property, so each placed instance supplies its own value while the definition stays untouched. The tempting reading — that changing the title edits the widget for everyone — is exactly what exposed properties exist to prevent.

options.label: Give each placed instance its own heading without editing the widget
Rename the widget itself from the page
Edit the widget's internal text component — changing every instance at once
Change the heading — which records a new widget version each time

challenges.prompt: You rework the Support Health Card: the progress bar becomes a trend chart and the On target badge disappears. Which version do you create?
challenges.explanation: Swapping the progress bar for a chart and dropping the badge changes what existing pages display — that's Major: a change in behavior or structure that existing uses should review. Minor is tempting because a chart feels additive, but Minor is for compatible additions; removing the badge makes this a review-worthy change, not an addition.

options.label: Major — existing uses should review the change
Minor — you added a chart, and additions are minor
Patch — the widget's job hasn't changed
No version needed — pages pick up widget edits either way

challenges.prompt: The card needs an Acknowledge button that different pages can wire to their own flows. Which steps are part of the correct setup?
challenges.explanation: The reusable contract has three parts: a named event in Widget Settings → Events, a widget_event action with that actionId on the button, and a binding to a workflow supplied where the widget is placed. Hardcoding workflow_event with a nodeId inside the definition is the tempting shortcut — it welds the widget to one flow, which is exactly the coupling widget events exist to avoid.

options.label: Define a named event in Widget Settings → Events
Give the button a widget_event action carrying that actionId
Bind the event to a workflow where the widget is placed
Point the button at the flow's node with workflow_event inside the widget definition
Duplicate the widget per page so each copy can target its own flow

challenges.prompt: Legal asks whether the "AI assistant — responses may need human review." pill in @ChatUI can be swapped for something friendlier. What do you tell them?
challenges.explanation: The disclosure text is yours to write — keep it direct or give it personality — but the disclosure itself stays visible so people know they're chatting with AI. Hiding it with custom CSS is the tempting route, and it's closed on purpose: chat CSS is sanitized and scoped, and no theme preset ships without the disclosure.

options.label: Yes — the wording is editable, but the disclosure itself stays visible
Yes — hide the pill with custom CSS
No — both the pill and its wording are fixed by Flow-Like
Yes — pick one of the theme presets that ships without it

challenges.prompt: You select Aurora Glass, then change --primary to brand purple. What does the theme selector show now — and what happens if you select Aurora Glass again?
challenges.explanation: Any edit to the copied CSS immediately flips the selector to Custom, and reselecting a preset replaces the editor contents with that preset's canonical source — your purple is gone. 'The variable merges into the preset' is the tempting mental model, but presets aren't layers: selecting one is a full copy, not a merge.

options.label: Custom — and reselecting the preset replaces the editor with its canonical CSS, discarding your change
Aurora Glass — your variable merges into the preset
Custom — and reselecting the preset re-applies it around your edit, keeping the purple
A new preset is saved under your app's name

challenges.prompt: A new hire asks how to open the assistant. What's the address, and why does it work?
challenges.explanation: The Chat UI Event owns the address: /chat resolves to that Event, and the Event opens the chat interface. Deriving routes from flow names is the tempting guess, but routes are configured on Events, never derived — and chat needs no page: the event type provides the whole interface.

options.label: /chat — the Chat UI Event's route resolves to that Event's interface
/customer-support-automation — routes derive from the flow name
It has no address until the chat is embedded on a Page
Chat UIs open at / by default

modules.title: Wire and ship
modules.description: Connect surfaces to flows with events, pin versions, and ship the console.

lessons.title: Connect UI to flows with events

challenges.prompt: What turns a Page button into "run the triage flow"?
challenges.explanation: Interactive components run flows through the fixed workflow_event action, which identifies the selected Event's node by nodeId. 'Buttons on a flow-owned page trigger that flow' is the tempting assumption — ownership links a page to its flow, but every click still needs an explicit action. Nothing fires by association.

options.label: A workflow_event action identifying the target event node by nodeId
An onClick handler written in the button's code panel
A navigate_page action pointing at the flow
Nothing extra — buttons on a flow-owned page trigger that flow

challenges.prompt: Customer Support Automation's conversational entry is a Chat Event node. Which Event types can invoke it?
challenges.explanation: The flow's entry node determines the Event types you can create: a Chat Event node supports Chat UI, Discord, and Telegram. Quick Action is the tempting universal answer, but it pairs with a Simple Event node — Event type and entry node must be compatible.

options.label: Chat UI, Discord, or Telegram
Quick Action — it's the universal UI type
Generic Form — a chat is a form with history
Any UI type — the Event adapts the payload to the node

challenges.prompt: The console goes to the whole support team tomorrow. Which are sound pre-ship moves?
challenges.explanation: Pin production events to numbered, immutable flow versions; test through the real routes end to end; make sure every UI event has a unique route and no red No route badge. Keeping Latest 'so fixes arrive instantly' is the tempting one — that's precisely how a Tuesday draft edit becomes the whole team's Tuesday incident. And backend-only events show no route because they don't need one; deleting them breaks the backend.

options.label: Pin the production events to a numbered, immutable flow version
Open /triage and /chat and run them end to end through the real events
Check every UI event has a unique route and no red No route badge
Keep events on Latest so this week's fixes reach the team instantly
Delete backend-only events, since they show no route

challenges.prompt: Checklist item 1: opening the app must land on the operations dashboard. What do you configure?
challenges.explanation: Routes live on UI Events, and / is the app's root — so the dashboard's Page-target Event takes route /. Reordering cards on the Pages tab is the tempting UI-first answer, but the Pages tab is a management list: card order affects nothing about navigation, and pages have no route setting of their own.

options.label: Give the dashboard's Page-target Event the route /
Rename the page to "/" in Page Settings
Move the dashboard to the first position on the Pages tab
Keep / on the chat and add a dashboard button to it

challenges.prompt: Checklist item 2: the health card on two pages, saying "Queue health" on one and "Escalation health" on the other. What's the right structure?
challenges.explanation: One widget, with the exposed Card title property supplying a different heading per instance — the definition stays shared, so improvements land everywhere. Two separate widgets is the tempting 'safe' answer, but it recreates the copy-paste drift problem widgets exist to solve; and versions are snapshots in time, not per-page variants.

options.label: One widget; each instance supplies its own Card title value
Two widgets, one per heading, so the pages stay independent
One widget, two versions — one version per page
One widget; edit the definition's heading depending on which page ships next

challenges.prompt: Checklist item 3: the Escalate button lives inside the health card widget and must run escalation logic in Customer Support Automation when pressed on the console. Which two pieces make that work?
challenges.explanation: The widget declares a named event its button triggers (widget_event with an actionId), and the console page's instance binds that event to the escalation workflow. Hardcoding the flow's nodeId in the definition is the tempting shortcut — it would make every future instance escalate, on every page, whether that page wants it or not. And navigate_page goes somewhere; it doesn't run anything.

options.label: A named widget event the button triggers via widget_event and its actionId
An action binding on the console's instance connecting that event to the flow
The flow's nodeId hardcoded in the widget definition
A navigate_page action pointing at /triage

challenges.prompt: Checklist item 4: Aurora Glass with brand purple, AI notice kept word for word. Feasible?
challenges.explanation: Feasible exactly as asked: select Aurora Glass (its full CSS is copied into the editor), change --primary — the selector flips to Custom, which is fine — and the disclosure stays visible with the wording legal approved. The trap is promising CSS can remove the pill later: chat CSS is sanitized and scoped, and the disclosure isn't removable.

options.label: Yes — copy the preset, edit --primary (the selector becomes Custom), keep the disclosure text as approved
No — preset CSS is read-only, so brand colors need a Page instead of chat
Yes — and if legal relents, custom CSS can remove the pill too
Partly — colors require rebuilding the chat from A2UI components

challenges.prompt: Checklist item 5: you keep improving the flow all week, but nothing the team uses may change before Friday. Which practices deliver that?
challenges.explanation: Pin the shipped events to a numbered, immutable flow version; keep editing the draft freely, because pinned events don't follow it; repoint the events to the new reviewed version on Friday. 'Latest freezes at publish time' is the tempting misread — Latest means the opposite: it follows the editable draft continuously, which is exactly what the requirement forbids.

options.label: Point the shipped events at a numbered flow version
Keep editing the draft — events pinned to a numbered version don't follow it
On Friday, repoint the events to the new reviewed version
Ship on Latest — it freezes at publish time
Numbered versions absorb draft edits automatically

challenges.prompt: Beta report: "Customer Intake shows on the Pages tab, but nobody can open it." Diagnosis?
challenges.explanation: A page becomes reachable through a UI Event with that page as its target and a unique route path — Customer Intake has none, so it's visible to builders and invisible to users. 'It was never saved' is the tempting explanation, but page changes save automatically after you stop editing; reachability, not persistence, is what's missing.

options.label: No UI Event exposes it — it needs a Page-target Event with a unique route
The page was never saved, so it exists half-created
Pages need publishing from the Pages tab before use
Its flow is deactivated, which hides the page

challenges.prompt: Friday retro — one teammate still wants a second engineer for "the chat codebase." Which statements about the console you shipped are true?
challenges.explanation: The dashboard, the widget, and any A2UI a flow returns share one component model; the chat needed configuration, not construction; every surface resolves path → Event → interface; and the Escalate behavior stayed out of the widget definition, bound by the page instead. The false one is subpath matching: routes match as configured — /chat doesn't answer /chat/anything. There is no separate chat codebase to staff.

options.label: The dashboard, the health card, and flow-returned interfaces share one component model
The chat needed no page building — its Event provides the interface
Every surface the team opens resolves through a path-to-Event mapping
The Escalate behavior stayed out of the widget definition, supplied by the page instead
Routes cover their subpaths, so /chat also answers /chat/history
